title: Arkaik ProjectBundle
description: The import/export format for an Arkaik product graph. Contains a project, its nodes (flows, views, data models, API endpoints), and edges (relationships between nodes).

schema_version.description: Bundle Format contract version. Absent means 1 (docs/spec/bundle-format.md § Schema Versioning). Older versions migrate through an explicit chain; unknown fields from newer versions are preserved on re-export.

nodes.description: All nodes in the project graph.

journal.description: Optional embedded journal events — the Level 2 interchange projection (docs/spec/journal.md). Canonical storage in repos is the JSONL sidecar; a bundle without a journal is Level 0/1, not an error.

quality.description: Optional Kritik quality state (docs/rfcs/kritik.md § 4.1) — the pinned pack version, the project's surface profile, its assessments and findings. Additive: a bundle without it is not an error, and the comparative matrix is derived from it (deriveQualityMatrix), never stored.

weighing.description: Optional weighing state (docs/rfcs/weighing.md) — the project's own criteria sets (a positioning), matrices and assessments, each assessment carrying its scorer, confidence and basis. Additive: a bundle without it is not an error, and every weight, served and cost figure is derived from it, never stored.

version.description: Current version label of the mapped product (free-form; semver recommended, not required). Version history lives in the journal as release.tagged events.

root_node_id.description: ID of the root node used as the canvas entry point. Should reference an existing node.

archived_at.description: ISO 8601 archive timestamp, or null if active.

maps.description: Stored map definitions (docs/spec/maps.md § Storage) — additive; unknown fields preserved.

map_display.description: Per-map display overrides keyed by map id (docs/spec/maps.md § Display Options) — the only path open to the built-in maps.

products.description: Product definitions (docs/spec/bundle-format.md § Products) — additive; unknown fields preserved.

pollen.description: Federation settings — docs/spec/services.md § Pollen feed. `plant` enables the feed.

id.description: Kebab-case, unique within the project; built-in ids (journey, system, screens) are reserved.

kind.description: Map kind: journey | system | screens. Selects the renderer and selection defaults; unrecognized kinds are preserved and listed as unrenderable.

species.description: Node filter; defaults by kind (journey: flow+view; system: view+api-endpoint+data-model; screens: flow+view).

edge_types.description: Edge filter; defaults by kind (journey: composes; system: calls+displays+queries; screens: none).

root_node_id.description: Scope anchor: the subgraph is the undirected neighborhood reachable from this node.

depth.description: Traversal bound from the root; absent = unbounded.

layout.description: Renderer layout hints (e.g. direction: DOWN | RIGHT).

display.description: Card rendering; the human twin is project.metadata.map_display[id].

images.description: Screenshot (or cover) art on view cards.

flow_platforms.description: A flow card's platform delivery: rings (default) | bars.

view_platforms.description: A view card's platform availability: chips (default) | rows.

minimap_color.description: What a minimap node's fill encodes: status (default) | species.

MapDisplayOptions.description: How a map draws its cards (docs/spec/maps.md § Display Options).

platforms.description: The platforms this product can ship on; empty means availability is not tracked.

id.description: Unique node ID. Convention: prefix with species — F- (flow), V- (view), DM- (data-model), API- (api-endpoint), AC- (acceptance), DEC- (decision), STK- (stake), OPT- (option).

description.description: Optional description of the node's purpose.

Species.description: The species of a node. flow = ordered sequence of views/sub-flows. view = reusable page or screen. data-model = data entity/table. api-endpoint = API endpoint. acceptance = a testable promise (one Given/When/Then) with per-platform status. decision = an ADR-style record (context, consequences, supersession). stake = something that matters about the product (a bug, friction, need, requirement, risk or defect), anchored to the anatomy by concerns edges. option = one way to address a stake, never without a stake, weighed against the other options for it.

AnyStatus.description: Lifecycle status as stored: the current vocabulary, or a legacy id (prioritized, blocked) accepted from pre-v3 bundles and migrated on load.

blocked_by.description: Non-empty = blocked at the current status. A node id (rendered as a link) or free text naming the dependency.

refs.description: Typed external references on the node.

gherkin.description: Acceptance nodes only: exactly one Given/When/Then scenario (the How). A second scenario is a second acceptance node.

values.description: Acceptance nodes only: 1..n Bain value elements served (the Why).

product.description: Product membership (docs/spec/bundle-format.md § Products); flow, view, and acceptance only.

decision_status.description: Decision nodes only: proposed | approved | enacted | rejected | deprecated | superseded. The node's lifecycle status is kept in sync (spec §2).

context.description: Decision nodes only: Context — the Why (markdown).

consequences.description: Decision nodes only: Consequences — the How (markdown).

decided_at.description: Decision nodes only: ISO 8601 date the decision was made.

stake_species.description: Stake nodes only: bug | friction | need | requirement | risk | defect.

provenance.description: Stake nodes only: observed (default when absent) or anticipated.

catalog.description: Stake nodes only: link into the Kritik criteria or the value pyramid, by id.

id.description: A Kritik criterion id (SAF-01) or a value id (reduces-anxiety). Nothing else is copied.

evidence.description: Stake nodes only: the signals behind the stake, one entry per signal. Written at qualification.

event_id.description: The journal event (a request.filed) the evidence came from.

quote.description: The line that matters, exactly as voiced.

voice.description: Who voiced it: person | maintainer | agent.

date.description: ISO 8601 date the evidence was voiced.

suggested_by.description: Option nodes only: the id of the request.filed journal event that seeded this option.

closed_options.description: Decision nodes only: the options that lost, each with the reason.

option_id.description: The id of the option that was not chosen.

PlaylistEntry.description: An entry in a flow's playlist. Discriminated union on 'type'.

PlatformStatusMap.description: Per-platform status overrides for view nodes.

PlatformScreenshotsMap.description: Per-platform screenshot: a relative path, an absolute URL, or a data URI (see docs/spec/bundle-format.md § Asset Values).

ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the current shot was recorded.

source.description: Who recorded the current shot: ci or manual.

form.description: Asset form of the slot value: url, path or data (see Asset Values).

commit.description: The sha a CI shot was rendered from.

order.description: That commit's height on the default branch.

ci_order.description: The highest CI order ever accepted for this slot, kept across a manual shot and a removal so a late CI re-run cannot overwrite a newer shot.

PlatformScreenshotMeta.description: Provenance of the current per-platform screenshot and the CI order watermark.

type.description: Ref type: figma | github-issue | gitlab-issue | linear-issue | github-pr | gitlab-mr | url. Unrecognized values are preserved and render as generic links.

status_mapped.description: Optional mapping of external_status into the arkaik lifecycle. Advisory display data — never mutates node.status.

platform.description: Optional scoping to one platform variant.

synced_at.description: ISO 8601 — when external_status was last mirrored.

Ref.description: A typed external reference on a node (docs/spec/bundle-format.md § References).

Value.description: A Bain B2C Elements-of-Value element served by an acceptance (spec §3.2).

DecisionStatus.description: Decision nodes only: proposed → approved (agreed, not yet reality) → enacted (in effect); terminal: rejected, deprecated, superseded. Not a lifecycle status — the node's status field is kept in sync (proposed→discovery, approved→backlog, enacted→live, terminals→archived).

StakeSpecies.description: Stake nodes only: bug | friction | need (user-facing, weighed on the value pyramid) or requirement | risk | defect (quality, read against Kritik criteria).

StakeProvenance.description: Stake nodes only: observed (seen in the world; the default when absent) or anticipated (reasoned about ahead of it; never a bug or a friction).

StakeCatalogSource.description: Where a stake's catalog link points: kritik (a criterion id such as SAF-01) or values (a value id such as reduces-anxiety).

StakeEvidenceVoice.description: Who voiced a piece of stake evidence: person (the one the signal came from), maintainer, or agent.

StakeFelt.description: Bug, friction and need stakes only: how the person feels it. expected (a must-be: a bug is always this), wanted (a performance) or delight (an attractive).

StakeMatters.description: Bug, friction and need stakes only: how much addressing it matters to the person, 4 (most) to 1 (least). Worded per felt kind; never summed with a pyramid level or a Kritik criticality.

StakeFrequency.description: Bug, friction and need stakes only: how often the situation comes up for the person: rare, some or often. Shown beside mattering, never sorted by.

EdgeType.description: composes = structural hierarchy (flow↔view). calls = view/flow → api-endpoint, or api-endpoint → api-endpoint (endpoint fan-out to internal/external APIs). displays = view → data-model. queries = api-endpoint → data-model. covers = acceptance → view/flow (which surface the acceptance is proven on). supersedes = decision → decision. generates = decision → acceptance or option (what the decision produced). impacts = decision → flow/view/data-model/api-endpoint or stake (what the decision acts on). concerns = stake → flow/view/data-model/api-endpoint (the part of the anatomy the stake is about). addresses = option → stake, acceptance → stake or acceptance → option (what answers a stake).

v.description: Reserved per-event payload version; absent today.

type.description: Event type — the v1 vocabulary in docs/spec/journal.md, or an unknown forward-compatible value.

JournalEvent.description: One append-only journal event. Type-specific payload fields sit flat on the object; unknown types and fields are preserved on rewrite (forward compatibility). See docs/spec/journal.md.

QualitySection.description: The project's Kritik state (docs/rfcs/kritik.md § 4.1) — profile, assessments, findings. Criteria are library content, not graph nodes; the matrix is a projection, never stored.

version.description: Semver of the pack; matrices are comparable only within a major.

KritikLibrary.description: A versioned criteria pack. Embedded on export; repos may instead pin it as a sidecar file.

KritikDomain.description: A top-level criteria category owning a roll-up row in the matrix.

id.description: Stable identifier, `<DOMAIN>-NN`. Never redefined — retired via superseded_by.

applies_to.description: Surface ids where the criterion is meaningful; absence means N/A.

level_anchors.description: Observable descriptions per maturity level, keyed l0…l4.

weight.description: Weight in the domain roll-up (1–3; 3 = load-bearing). Absent means 1.

signals.description: Mechanically checkable monitoring hooks run between audits.

KritikReference.description: A stable external anchor behind a criterion (OWASP control, GDPR article, WCAG SC…).

KritikIssueTemplate.description: Per-criterion issue skeleton — what `arkaik kritik issue` prefills.

KritikScales.description: Overridable maturity/severity/grade scales carried by a criteria pack. Absent entries fall back to the framework defaults (packages/kritik-library/SPEC.md § 4).

domain_weights.description: Per-domain weight in the surface roll-up, keyed by domain code. A missing weight is 1.

QualityProfile.description: The project's parameterization of the pack (RFC § 6).

platform.description: Optional bridge to PLATFORM_IDS where a surface is also a view-shipping platform. Surfaces are not platforms (RFC § 2).

SurfaceDef.description: One independently assessable body of code — an audit target, chosen at install.

level.description: Maturity 0–4. N/A is the absence of the row, never a level.

evidence.description: file:line / config citations. A score without evidence is an opinion, not an assessment.

QualityAssessment.description: One (criterion × surface) score — latest wins; history lives in the journal.

node_ids.description: Graph nodes this finding is about — the tie deliverable.shipped already uses.

commit.description: Commit SHA anchoring the file:line evidence. Required by policy on any finding written away from a checkout (issue #400 decision 4) — without it a stale citation is indistinguishable from a wrong one.

verification.description: Result of the adversarial refutation pass. Refuted findings are disclosed, not deleted.

QualityFinding.description: One concrete defect. Severity and priority are deliberately absent — they are derived from impact × likelihood and cost (deriveQualityMatrix), so a finding can never carry a severity its own numbers disagree with.

WeighingSection.description: The project's weighing state (docs/rfcs/weighing.md) — its own criteria sets (a positioning), matrices and assessments. The built-in value set is library content, not stored; served, cost and kept share are derived, never stored. Each list may be absent; a reader treats it as empty.

version.description: Semver. Levels are comparable only within a major.

subject.description: What the set judges: acceptance today.

stake_species.description: The kinds of stake this set may also score (bug, friction, need, requirement, risk, defect). Absent means none; the value ruler declares bug, friction and need.

scale.description: The scale. A positioning may leave it out and use its ruler's.

role.description: positioning marks the set a project writes about itself.

status.description: Absent or active is active; anything else is a draft, which feeds no roll-up.

WeighingCriteriaSet.description: A versioned list of criteria for one kind of subject. The 30 elements of value are one; a positioning is another.

anchors.description: Every level described in words, keyed by the level as a string.

WeighingScale.description: A criteria set's scale: its bounds and every level's anchor.

WeighingGroup.description: A grouping of criteria — the tiers, for the value set.

id.description: Stable identifier. Never redefined — retired via superseded_by.

group.description: A group id — for the value set, the tier.

anchors.description: This criterion's own wording of each level — on a positioning, in the product's words.

weight.description: On a positioning: how much the product stands on it, a number above 0. Absent means 1.

superseded_by.description: The id of the criterion that replaces this one.

WeighingCriterion.description: One question on a scale where every level is described.

set.description: The set's id and major, e.g. value-contribution@2.

subjects.description: What the matrix judges: { kind: query, species } or { kind: list, items }.

species.description: For a query: the species judged.

positioning.description: The id of the positioning set that re-weights this matrix.

context.description: The node the matrix is about, as { node_id }.

status.description: Absent or active is active; anything else is a draft.

WeighingMatrix.description: A criteria set applied to a list of subjects.

matrix.description: The matrix's id. A row without it cannot be addressed: readers skip it and the validator warns.

subject.description: A node id for the value matrix.

level.description: A whole number on the set's scale. 0 means unrelated. No half points — but any value parses; the validator warns on one off the scale.

scorer.description: Who judged. Required in practice: without it a human, an agent and a rule are indistinguishable, so the validator warns.

refs.description: Ids cited: nodes, journal events, findings.

basis.description: What the scorer was looking at, so a re-read can tell the score went stale.

fingerprint.description: A hash of the subject's judged fields.

commit.description: The commit the scorer was looking at.

set_version.description: The full version of the set the level was read against.

run.description: The audit or plan the score belongs to.

p_serves.description: Optional: a probabilistic scorer's certainty (0 to 1) that the subject serves the element. Certainty, not size. Any value parses; the validator warns on one outside 0..1.

p_costs.description: Optional: the same for costs, asked independently, so both can be high.

WeighingAssessment.description: One (matrix × subject × criterion) judgement — latest per scorer kind wins; history lives in the journal.

kind.description: Who judged: human, agent or rule. A human's level beats an agent's, which beats a rule's. Any value parses; the validator warns on another kind.

id.description: A person's handle, an agent's name, or a seeding rule's id.

model.description: The model behind an agent, when it says.

on_behalf_of.description: Whom the scorer acts for: a user id, a handle or a display name, never an email. Stamped by the writer where identity is known.
